When using the `get!` inline macro in Dojo, if a user provides a keys tuple whose length doesn't match the number of `#[key]` fields in the model struct, the deserialization fails with a generic error message like "Model failed to deserialize". This makes debugging difficult, as the user has to manually figure out that the issue is related to key length mismatch.

    The goal is to improve the error message produced by the `get!` macro when model deserialization fails. The new message should:
    - Clearly indicate that the model deserialization failed
    - Explicitly tell the user to check that the length of their keys tuple matches the number of `#[key]` fields in the model struct
    - Include the model name for context

    This will help developers quickly identify and fix common mistakes when calling `get!` with incorrect key tuples.

    The change should be minimal and focused on the `get!` macro's generated code and its corresponding semantic test expectations.

## Environment Setup
Check the following files to understand the build and test setup:
    - `Cargo.toml` (workspace root — lists all crates and shared dependencies)
    - `crates/dojo-lang/Cargo.toml` (specific crate manifest)
    - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (CI configuration showing how the project is built and tested)
    - `scripts/cargo_bench.sh`, `scripts/clippy.sh`, `scripts/rust_fmt.sh`, `scripts/cairo_test.sh` (helper scripts for various dev tasks)
    - `rust-toolchain.toml` (Rust toolchain pinning)
    - `crates/dojo-lang/README.md` (crate-specific notes)

## Implementation Plan
1. Edit `crates/dojo-lang/src/inline_macros/get.rs` to modify the `deser_err_msg` construction in the `generate_code` method of `GetMacro`.
    2. Replace the current truncated error message (e.g., `"Model failed to deserialize"`) with a more descriptive message that includes:
       - The model name
       - A clear statement that deserialization failed

21:                 match extract_models(db, &element) {

23:                     Err(diagnostic) => return Err(diagnostic),

26:         }

28:             match extract_models(db, &parenthesized.expr(db)) {

30:                 Err(diagnostic) => return Err(diagnostic),

        "message": "fix(core): upgrade checks for key members (#3285)\n\nIn the way we check if a model can be upgraded, some cases for `key` members are not well managed.\n\nHere are the `key` member upgrade rules that are checked according to the `key` member type:\n- `Primitive`: same than for a `value` member, the new type must have the same or a bigger size than the old type (`u8` -> `u16`),\n- `Struct`: new members are NOT allowed. Existing member types must follow the `key` member upgrade rules,\n- `Enum`: new variants are allowed. Existing variant data types must follow the `key` member upgrade rules,\n- `Tuple`: tuple items must follow the `key` member upgrade rules and the tuple size must remain the same,\n- `Fixed-Size Array`: the array item type must follow the `key` member upgrade rules and the array size must remain the same,\n- `Array`: the array item type must follow the `key` member upgrade rules,\n- `ByteArray`: always allowed.\n\n## Model reading with enum/option key\n\nSince the introduction of `DojoStore`, when a model is read, keys are serialized using `Serde` but read values were serialized with `DojoStore`. That means, when we try to deserialize the whole data keys+values using `DojoStore` it fails due to the fact that `Serde` and `DojoStore` don't handle variant indexes the same way.\n\nSo, this commit updates the `ModelParser::deserialize()` function to:\n- still use `Serde` to deserialize events and legacy models,\n- deserialize field by field, using `Serde` for key fields and `DojoStore` for value fields.\n\n---------\n\nCo-authored-by: Ammar Arif <evergreenkary@gmail.com>",

101:         }
102:         let hex_part = str_val.trim_start_matches("0x");
103:         let trimmed_hex = hex_part.trim_start_matches('0');
104:         Value::String(format!("0x{:0>1}", trimmed_hex))

118:         .map(|(field_name, type_data)| {
119:             let mut value =
120:                 fetch_value(row, field_name, &type_data.type_ref().to_string(), is_external)?;
121: 
122:             // handles felt arrays stored as string (ex: keys)
123:             if let (TypeRef::List(_), Value::String(s)) = (&type_data.type_ref(), &value) {
124:                 let mut felts: Vec<_> = s.split(FELT_DELIMITER).map(Value::from).collect();
125:                 felts.pop(); // removes empty item
126:                 value = Value::List(felts);
127:             }
128: 
129:             Ok((Name::new(field_name), value))
130:         })
131:         .collect::<sqlx::Result<ValueMapping>>()?;
132:

134:     if let Ok(entity_id) = row.try_get::<String, &str>(ENTITY_ID_COLUMN) {
135:         value_mapping.insert(Name::new(INTERNAL_ENTITY_ID_KEY), Value::from(entity_id));

144:     type_name: &str,
145:     is_external: bool,
146: ) -> sqlx::Result<Value> {

148:         if is_external { format!("external_{}", field_name) } else { field_name.to_string() };
149: 
150:     match Primitive::from_str(type_name) {

152:         Ok(Primitive::Bool(_)) => {
153:             Ok(Value::from(matches!(row.try_get::<i64, &str>(&column_name)?, BOOLEAN_TRUE)))
154:         }
155:         // fetch integer/string base on sql type
156:         Ok(ty) => match ty.to_sql_type() {
157:             SqlType::Integer => row.try_get::<i64, &str>(&column_name).map(Value::from),
158:             SqlType::Text => Ok(remove_hex_leading_zeros(
159:                 row.try_get::<String, &str>(&column_name).map(Value::from)?,
160:             )),
161:         },
162:         // fetch everything else as non-formated string

22: // The graphql schema is built dynamically at runtime, this is because we won't know the schema of
23: // the models until runtime. There are however, predefined objects such as entities and
24: // events, their schema is known but we generate them dynamically as well because async-graphql
25: // does not allow mixing of static and dynamic schemas.
26: pub async fn build_schema(pool: &SqlitePool) -> Result<Schema> {
27:     // build world gql objects
28:     let (objects, union) = build_objects(pool).await?;
29: 
30:     // collect resolvers for single and plural queries
31:     let queries: Vec<Field> = objects
32:         .iter()
33:         .flat_map(|object| vec![object.resolve_one(), object.resolve_many()].into_iter().flatten())
34:         .collect();
35: 
36:     // add field resolvers to query root
37:     let mut query_root = Object::new(QUERY_TYPE_NAME);
38:     for query in queries {
39:         query_root = query_root.field(query);
40:     }
41: 
42:     let mut schema_builder = Schema::build(QUERY_TYPE_NAME, None, Some(SUBSCRIPTION_TYPE_NAME));
43: 
44:     // register model data unions
45:     schema_builder = schema_builder.register(union);
46: 
47:     // register default scalars
48:     for scalar_type in ScalarType::all().iter() {
49:         schema_builder = schema_builder.register(Scalar::new(scalar_type));
50:     }
51: 
52:     for object in &objects {
53:         // register enum objects
54:         if let Some(input_objects) = object.enum_objects() {
55:             for input in input_objects {
56:                 schema_builder = schema_builder.register(input);
57:             }
58:         }
59: 
60:         // register input objects, whereInput and orderBy
61:         if let Some(input_objects) = object.input_objects() {
62:             for input in input_objects {
63:                 schema_builder = schema_builder.register(input);
64:             }
65:         }
66: 
67:         // register connection types, relay
68:         if let Some(conn_objects) = object.connection() {
69:             for object in conn_objects {
70:                 schema_builder = schema_builder.register(object);
71:             }
72:         }
73: 
74:         // register gql objects
75:         let object_collection = object.objects();
76:         for object in object_collection {
77:             schema_builder = schema_builder.register(object);
78:         }
79:     }
80: 
81:     // collect resolvers for single subscriptions
82:     let mut subscription_fields: Vec<SubscriptionField> = Vec::new();
83:     for object in &objects {
84:         if let Some(subscriptions) = object.subscriptions() {
85:             for sub in subscriptions {
86:                 subscription_fields.push(sub);
87:             }
88:         }
89:     }
90: 
91:     // add field resolvers to subscription root
92:     let mut subscription_root = Subscription::new(SUBSCRIPTION_TYPE_NAME);
93:     for field in subscription_fields {
94:         subscription_root = subscription_root.field(field);
95:     }
96: 
97:     schema_builder
98:         .register(query_root)
99:         .register(subscription_root)
100:         .data(pool.clone())
101:         .finish()
102:         .map_err(|e| e.into())
103: }

105: async fn build_objects(pool: &SqlitePool) -> Result<(Vec<Box<dyn ObjectTrait>>, Union)> {
106:     let mut conn = pool.acquire().await?;
107:     let models: Vec<Model> = sqlx::query_as("SELECT * FROM models").fetch_all(&mut conn).await?;
108: 
109:     // predefined objects
110:     let mut objects: Vec<Box<dyn ObjectTrait>> = vec![
111:         Box::new(EntityObject),
112:         Box::new(EventObject),
113:         Box::new(SocialObject),
114:         Box::new(ContentObject),
115:         Box::new(MetadataObject),
116:         Box::new(ModelObject),
117:         Box::new(PageInfoObject),
118:         Box::new(TransactionObject),
119:     ];
120: 
121:     // model union object
122:     let mut union = Union::new("ModelUnion");
123: 
124:     // model data objects
125:     for model in models {
126:         let type_mapping = type_mapping_query(&mut conn, &model.id).await?;
127: 
128:         if !type_mapping.is_empty() {
129:             let field_name = model.name.to_lowercase();
130:             let type_name = model.name;
131: 
132:             union = union.possible_type(&type_name);
133: 
134:             objects.push(Box::new(ModelDataObject::new(field_name, type_name, type_mapping)));
135:         }
136:     }
137: 
138:     Ok((objects, union))
139: }

1: # Dojo ECS Example
2: 
3: This repo contains a simple example of using the Dojo ECS system. It defines a simple game where a player has a limited set of moves and can move their position through executing the move system.
4: 
5: ## Getting started
6: 
7: ```sh
8: # Build the world
9: sozo build
10: 
11: # Migrate the world
12: sozo migrate
13: 
14: # Get the class hash of the Moves model by name
15: sozo model class-hash --world 0x26065106fa319c3981618e7567480a50132f23932226a51c219ffb8e47daa84 Moves
16: > 0x2b97f0b24be59ecf4504a27ac2301179be7df44c4c7d9482cd7b36137bc0fa4
17: 
18: # Get the schema of the Moves model
19: sozo model schema --world 0x26065106fa319c3981618e7567480a50132f23932226a51c219ffb8e47daa84 Moves
20: > struct Moves {
21: >    remaining: u8
22: > }
23: 
24: # Get the value of the Moves model for an entity. (in this example,
25: # 0x517ececd29116499f4a1b64b094da79ba08dfd54a3edaa316134c41f8160973 is
26: # the calling account.
27: sozo model get --world 0x26065106fa319c3981618e7567480a50132f23932226a51c219ffb8e47daa84 Moves 0x517ececd29116499f4a1b64b094da79ba08dfd54a3edaa316134c41f8160973
28: > 0x0
29: 
30: # The returned value is 0 since we haven't spawned yet. 
31: # We can spawn a player using the actions contract address
32: sozo execute 0x31571485922572446df9e3198a891e10d3a48e544544317dbcbb667e15848cd spawn
33: 
34: # Fetch the updated entity
35: sozo model get --world 0x26065106fa319c3981618e7567480a50132f23932226a51c219ffb8e47daa84 Moves 0x517ececd29116499f4a1b64b094da79ba08dfd54a3edaa316134c41f8160973
36: > 0xa
37: ```
